{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABiAbYxQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhLYLX0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 138, "title": "Remember user-imported ROMs in IndexedDB and add a reusable cartridge picker", "body": "## Problem

The current web player remembers cartridge saves (SRAM/EEPROM), console EEPROM, RTC records and audio/display preferences, but not the user's ROM files. After reloading or revisiting the site, the user must find and select the same local `.ws` / `.wsc` file again. This is particularly inconvenient on phones.

Implement the same user-facing convenience as the sibling project's [snes-rust Issue #170](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/170) and [PR #171](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/pull/171): remember successfully imported personal ROMs in browser-local IndexedDB and let the user select them from a compact cartridge picker on subsequent visits.

The WonderSwan player must remain **user-ROM-only** as established by #108 / #109. Do not reintroduce a demo, bundled game, remote ROM catalog, account or server.

## Expected outcome

- Opening a new valid local ROM starts it using the existing loader and automatically remembers the ROM and its filename in this browser. No separate Save ROM button or additional import confirmation is needed. Make the local retention behavior clear in a short help/README explanation and allow removal.
- On a subsequent visit, the player still starts with no cartridge inserted and no automatic playback. The user can choose a remembered cartridge without reopening the operating system file picker. Selecting it loads the stored bytes, restores its existing cartridge save and RTC data, and starts play subject to the same model, visibility, focus and audio policies as a new local import.
- Provide one compact cartridge picker in the existing cartridge area: remembered entries under **My cartridges** when nonempty, a per-entry **Remove** action, and an always-available **Open local ROM…** action. Keep the current cartridge name and Console selector outside the picker. Integrate with the recently merged #136 / #137 layout.
- ROM persistence is best-effort and independent of cartridge progress. If the database cannot remember a ROM, an otherwise valid local ROM remains playable; the user receives a concise, actionable warning. Never advertise a successful stored entry before its transaction commits.
- Removing a remembered ROM deletes only the browser's stored copy and metadata, not the original file, cartridge SRAM/EEPROM, RTC, console EEPROM or user preferences. Removing the currently inserted ROM must not eject, restart, interrupt or otherwise change the running or paused game.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline checked at `main` commit [bb6f672](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/commit/bb6f672a1ec40dd688d01a1f6b312b28ad8e7359) (merged layout PR #137). Inspect current main again before editing.

- [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/index.html) and [`web/src/style.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/style.css): the light-theme cartridge panel currently contains the inserted filename, Load ROM button and Console selector. Add the picker here without expanding the main toolbar or introducing a permanent library page.
- [`web/src/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/main.ts): `load(name, bytes, key, autoplay)`, `readROM(name, read)`, `readRevision`, `visibilityRevision`, `persist()`, `restoreClock()`, `restoreConsole()`, local file input, `sound.unlock()`, `focusGame()`, model restart and Help/fullscreen/input lifecycle. Reuse this loading pipeline for both local files and remembered entries. Current file-size precheck is 64 MiB (mapper dependent); the core remains the authority on actual valid cartridge size/header/model.
- [`web/src/saves.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/saves.ts): `romIdentity(bytes)` hashes the **entire original raw ROM contents** to produce `wonderswan:save:v1:<sha256>`. Cartridge saves, physical-model console EEPROM and RTC records have established independent keys and storage-failure policies. Preserve all of them. Unlike the SNES project, WonderSwan has no copier-header normalization requirement; do not strip, pad, normalize, or otherwise transform ROM bytes for identity or storage.
- [`web/scripts/smoke.mjs`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/scripts/smoke.mjs), [`web/scripts/compat.mjs`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/scripts/compat.mjs), `keypad.mjs`, `lcd-output.mjs`, `console.mjs`, `rtc-calendar.mjs` and other current browser checks cover the real production player. Use existing source-included CC0 hardware fixtures loaded through the normal file input; no commercial ROM or physical device is required.
- Follow the [UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), and [test/CI performance principles](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md#test-and-ci-performance-principles).

### Sibling-project reference and lessons

Read [snes-rust #170](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/170) and the latest available [PR #171](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/pull/171), particularly its `web/app.js`, `web/index.html`, `web/style.css` and `web/tests/rom-library.spec.js` changes. PR #171 was still open at the time of planning (head `0323add2759e1fecb06e563633769a452ab0251d`), so use it as a design reference, not as a dependency or proof that all edge cases are resolved.

Relevant lessons from its review fixes: keep progress saves independent of library storage, do not reset an identical active cartridge, validate stored identities and bytes, allow removal/reimport of broken entries, prevent repeated Remove gestures from launching a different cartridge, and ensure storage warnings remain discoverable at narrow viewport sizes and after reopening the picker. Adapt these to WonderSwan's existing behavior rather than importing SNES-specific bundled demos, normalized hashes, SRAM safety gates, controller mappings or UI architecture.

### UX and layout

Use the existing cartridge panel as the sole entry point. Rename its primary button to **Insert cartridge** (or an equally concise cartridge-selection label), opening a lightweight accessible picker/popover/dialog. Example:

```text
Cartridge
No ROM loaded
[Insert cartridge]
Console [SwanCrystal v]

Picker:
  My cartridges
  [Example A.wsc]      [Remove]
  [Example B.ws]       [Remove]
  [Open local ROM…]
```

When empty, omit the empty library section or use one short empty-state message; always offer the local file action. No cover art, folders, tags, ROM renaming or extra permanent settings. Long filenames must be readable through truncation/full accessible name or wrapping without resizing the screen or obscuring Remove. Make the list scroll within the available viewport. Provide keyboard navigation, Escape/dismiss, outside dismissal where appropriate, focus restoration, and clear accessible names for removal; keep repeated Enter, double-click and double-tap from accidentally deleting or launching another entry when rows shift.

Opening/canceling the picker or canceling the native file chooser must not reset the current game or change its prior Play/Pause state. Respect current input isolation and clear stale held inputs when moving focus out of gameplay. Do not force an automatic restart on choosing/importing the same currently inserted ROM identity; leave the active state intact and repair its library record if necessary. Restart remains an explicit action. If an entry is incompatible with the currently selected console, use the existing validation/error path; do not silently change model or discard the current game. Preserve the newly redesigned desktop layout, mobile portrait/short-landscape controls, rotated cartridges and fullscreen behavior. Avoid unnecessary new scroll or screen resizing when library metadata changes.

### Storage, validation and lifecycle

1. Use a small, well-defined TypeScript IndexedDB module/helper, with a **project-specific database name**, e.g. `wonderswan-rust:cartridges`, version 1. Both sibling Pages sites share the same web origin, so database names/object-store conventions must not collide with the SNES project's `snes-rust:cartridges`. Namespace separation prevents accidental mixing; it is not an independent browser security boundary. Do not modify the other project's database.
2. Store the actual binary ROM bytes (ArrayBuffer/typed array/Blob), exact raw SHA-256 identity and minimal metadata (filename, optionally size). Never base64-encode ROMs into localStorage. Store metadata separately from large binary values or use an equivalent lightweight indexed projection: startup/picker enumeration must not read all ROM byte arrays into memory or Wasm. Fetch one binary on explicit selection only.
3. Deduplicate by the existing full raw-content SHA-256, not filename. Same bytes under another name produce one entry; keep a deterministic display-name policy. Same filename with different contents produces distinct entries and distinct save identities. Reimport can repair a damaged/missing record without duplicate entries. Preserve raw bytes for 3/6 MiB top-aligned images and all other supported formats.
4. Only remember local imports **after successful acceptance by the normal core loading/validation path**. Invalid, unsupported, incompatible or oversized files must not create library entries. The already-inserted identical ROM is already validated; reimporting it may repair/persist its entry without restarting. A ROM storage-write failure must not convert a successful load into an emulator execution failure.
5. On selecting a remembered entry, validate metadata/identity format and bounded byte length, recompute its raw hash, check that it matches the expected identity, and use the same validation, save/RTC restoration, and model/orientation pipeline as a file import. Do not trust IndexedDB bytes or use filename as identity. Missing, malformed or corrupt records must remain removable and recoverable by reimport; malformed filenames should have a safe fallback label.
6. Treat **transaction completion**, not request success, as the durable-write/delete boundary. Keep metadata/binary updates atomic and the list consistent after aborted transactions, duplicate imports, concurrent changes or reloads. Use the existing read revision/visibility guards or an equivalent bounded approach so stale async selection results cannot replace a newer game, restart behind Help/hidden state, steal focus or change current cartridge unexpectedly. Use identity-based removal, not row position or filename. Refresh list when needed to reflect cross-tab changes; no realtime sync system is required.
7. Preserve existing cartridge-save, RTC and console-EEPROM read/write behavior, keys, corruption safeguards and notices. Do not migrate or delete those records with the library. Flush progress through existing lifecycle paths on switching/restarting/pausing; library failures have separate feedback and must not erase or mask progress-storage errors. Do not introduce SNES-specific changes to WonderSwan's existing save-failure policy as part of this task.
8. Handle IndexedDB unavailable/denied, open/upgrade errors, blocked database, quota exhaustion, transaction abort, missing/corrupt bytes, and deletion failure without preventing local-file gameplay. Show a concise warning with an obvious recovery route (free site storage, reopen original file, or remove broken entry as applicable). A failed write must not create a false saved entry, a failed removal must not claim success, and successful retry clears the relevant library warning. Keep the warning accessible in a reopened picker without permanently cluttering the gameplay area.
9. Privacy: never transmit ROM bytes, filenames/library metadata, saves or RTC data to a server. The app remains static GitHub Pages; no account, cloud sync, upload API, remote assets or new network service. Browser storage is best-effort and may be cleared/evicted or unavailable in private mode. Keep original files separately. Do not silently request filesystem access or persistent-storage permission; storing a local browser copy is sufficient.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement the compact cartridge picker in the existing light-theme cartridge area. A fresh visitor starts empty, can import a local supported ROM, and sees one remembered entry only after the actual IndexedDB transaction completes. Reload and reopen the same browser profile/origin; choosing the remembered ROM plays the actual stored bytes without a native file chooser or network request. No automatic cartridge boot on startup.
- [ ] Use a WonderSwan-specific versioned IndexedDB database, store binary bytes directly and use the **unchanged full raw SHA-256** identity shared with existing save keys. Verify identical bytes/different names deduplicate; same-name/different bytes stay distinct; metadata enumeration does not read all stored ROM bodies. No SNES copier-header processing or database collision.
- [ ] Exercise the same real Wasm loading path for local and stored ROMs on the selected supported console. Reject invalid/incompatible/oversized imports without adding entries. Corrupt/missing/mismatched stored bytes must not boot or replace the active cartridge; they can be removed or repaired by reopening the original file. Reimport/select of an identical currently inserted ROM does not reset it.
- [ ] With existing CC0 save/RTC fixtures, verify a game's progress survives switching cartridges, reload and selecting a remembered ROM; deleting a remembered ROM and reimporting its exact bytes retains SRAM/EEPROM and RTC records. Removing the active entry does not change running/paused state, frame counter, inserted ROM, or console data. Preserve separate per-model console EEPROM and sound/display preferences.
- [ ] Test unavailable/denied IndexedDB, quota/transaction abort and missing/corrupt records (including malformed metadata), failed removal and successful retry. The normal local file route continues to work, list state reflects committed transactions only, and library warnings remain distinct from progress-save errors. Test representative overlapping reads/import/remove operations and stale completions without destructive cross-entry behavior.
- [ ] Verify keyboard/touch picker use, Escape/cancel, focus restoration, accessible per-entry removal, repeated removal gestures, long filenames/list scrolling, desktop and representative 375px portrait/short-landscape mobile viewports. The newly merged layout, both cartridge orientations, touch keypads, fullscreen, live display modes (Retro CRT default), audio unlock/mute, and Help/Debug behavior remain intact.
- [ ] Use request instrumentation to demonstrate that local imports and remembered-ROM use do not upload/fetch ROM content, filenames, saves or library metadata; retain the existing production Pages subpath and no-bundled-ROM output checks.
- [ ] Add focused real IndexedDB/real Wasm browser tests to existing production-preview suites (a small `web/scripts/rom-library.mjs` helper is acceptable). Prefer existing CC0 fixtures and targeted failure injection, not a new game or redundant exhaustive test matrix. Run applicable `npm ci`, `npm run build:wasm` if needed, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run test:compat` and `git diff --check`; report actual results and limitations. Run Rust/fixture checks only when their sources change or applicable regression coverage requires them.
- [ ] Update README and concise Help text to explain remembered ROMs, picking/removing them, local-only storage, and that clearing site data can erase both ROM copies and progress. Preserve the original files recommendation and the user-ROM-only product. No core changes, bundled games, new dependency/framework, save-state system or unrelated UI refactor.

## Optional validation

- Verify retention across a full browser-process restart using a persistent test profile, and exercise mobile WebKit/Safari and a larger supported raw ROM where practical. No requirement for a physical phone, proprietary ROM, or subjective human approval.

## Required post-merge verification

After all applicable pre-merge acceptance passes, merge and close the Issue in accordance with the repository lifecycle. Then verify the GitHub Pages deployment of the merge commit and record the run URL and deployed revision. On the published site, import a source-included CC0 fixture from a local file, reload, select it from My cartridges, remove/reimport it, and verify save retention and no ROM network requests. Record actual browser observations and any limitations. Treat a confirmed production regression as a separate linked Issue; do not reopen completed work simply because post-merge checks are pending.
